title: Understanding Training, Validation, and Test Data
introduction: This lesson explains why we split data into training, validation, and test sets, and introduces key ideas like generalization, overfitting, and data leakage.

sections.heading: Training Data
sections.subheading: The data that teaches the model
paragraphs: Training data contains input examples and their correct answers. The model looks at these pairs to learn patterns.
During learning the model adjusts its internal parameters to reduce errors on this data.

example.title: Handwritten digit recognition
example.content: A model learns to recognize digits by looking at many labeled images of handwritten numbers.

sections.heading: Validation Data
sections.subheading: How we tune the model while training
paragraphs: Validation data is separate from training data and is used to check how well the model is learning.
We use it to decide when to stop training or to choose the best model among many.

example.title: Choosing the best model
example.content: After each training epoch we compute accuracy on validation images to see if the model improves, then we may stop early if performance stops rising.

sections.heading: Test Data
paragraphs: Test data is never used during training or validation. It provides an unbiased estimate of real‑world performance.
After the model is finalized, we report its accuracy on the test set as the final result.

example.title: Final report
example.content: We evaluate the digit‑recognition model on a separate set of images that were never seen before and report the accuracy as the model’s true capability.

sections.heading: Generalization, Overfitting, and Data Leakage
sections.subheading: Why unseen data matters and common pitfalls
paragraphs: Generalization means the model works well on new, unseen data, not just the data it trained on.
Overfitting happens when the model memorizes training examples and fails on new data.
Data leakage occurs when information from the test set unintentionally influences training, giving overly optimistic results.

example.title: Overfitting example
example.content: A model that scores 100% on training data but only 60% on test data has overfitted. If test labels were accidentally included in training, the reported performance would be misleading due to data leakage.

practice.title: Simple data split exercise
practice.instruction: Take a list of 20 numbers. Write down 14 numbers as the training set, 4 numbers as the validation set, and 2 numbers as the test set. Explain why keeping these sets separate helps evaluate the model fairly.

keyTakeaways: Training data teaches the model by providing examples and correct answers.
Validation data helps tune the model and prevents over‑training.
Test data gives an unbiased measure of how the model will perform on new data.
Good generalization means the model works well on unseen data.
Data leakage can falsely inflate performance and must be avoided.

mcqs.question: What is the main role of training data in machine learning?
options: It provides examples and correct answers for the model to learn patterns.
It is used to evaluate the final performance of the model.
It helps decide when to stop training.
It prevents the model from overfitting.
mcqs.explanation: Training data contains input‑output pairs that the model uses to adjust its parameters and learn.

mcqs.question: Which data set is typically used to decide when to stop training or to choose the best model version?
options: Training set
Validation set
Test set
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The validation set is separate from training data and is consulted during training to monitor performance and trigger early stopping.

mcqs.question: What does the term 'overfitting' describe?
options: The model works well on new, unseen data.
The model memorizes training examples and performs poorly on new data.
The model has data leakage from the test set.
The model under‑learns and has low training accuracy.
mcqs.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model fits the training data too closely, losing its ability to generalize to unseen data.

mcqs.question: Which situation is an example of data leakage?
options: Including test labels in the training process.
Randomly splitting the data into three sets.
Using the validation set to stop training early.
Training only on the training set without any validation.
mcqs.explanation: Data leakage happens when information from the test set (e.g., labels) unintentionally influences training, inflating performance metrics.

mcqs.question: Why must test data be kept completely separate from training and validation data?
options: To provide an unbiased estimate of real‑world performance.
To tune hyper‑parameters during model development.
To keep a completely unseen set for the final evaluation.
To reduce the amount of computation needed during training.
mcqs.explanation: Test data is never used during model building; it serves as a final, unseen benchmark to measure true capability.
